title: Identity write request v1
description: Three writes. `fgos identity machine --alias <name>` replaces <stateRoot>/machine-alias atomically; the alias must follow the Convention machine-handle kind, changes the handle only, never the machine id, and needs a machine id to exist. `fgos identity project --init|--new [--handle <name>]` writes .fgos/project.json of the main checkout: `--init` mints once and refuses when the file exists (project-id-exists), in a linked worktree (linked-worktree) or when the remote default branch, as last fetched, already tracks the file (project-id-on-remote); `--new` replaces the id on purpose (a fork split) and skips the last two checks. The handle follows the Convention project-handle kind and defaults to the slug of the folder name. Nothing else ever writes the file. `fgos identity mint <kind> [--release <number>]` mints an id that travels between machines (docs/platform/identity/spec.md, section 4a): `work` gives `tsk-<10 base32>` and `backlog` gives `p-<10 base32>` from the kernel's random bytes and writes nothing; `d-adr` and `decision-file` claim the next number of the counter ref `refs/fgos/seq/<kind>` on the project's `origin` (the repository's own ref when it has none), one more than the larger of the counter and the highest number the repository's documents carry, retrying a refused compare-and-swap up to 5 times. `--release <number>` gives a sequence number back, only while it is still the counter's tip. Without a network the claim is refused (`sequence-unreachable`); the format is never changed to work around it.

outcome.title: Identity write outcome v1
outcome.description: The machine as `identity.read` prints it after an alias write, the project minted with where it went and the command that commits it, the id minted, or the answer to a release.

commit.description: The command that commits the new file by pathspec.

released.description: false when somebody claimed after, so the counter stays.
